summary: FESS in a patient with aspirin exacerbated respiratory disease whose allergy was downgraded to GI upset in 2022; the ENT order set has ketorolac and ibuprofen ordered, he bronchospasmed after ketorolac in 2020, and his Samter's bracelet is in a belongings bag.

asa.rationale: Moderate persistent asthma with wheeze, AERD, mild OSA.

decision.rationale: Cancel ketorolac and ibuprofen, correct the allergy entry, use acetaminophen and celecoxib per allergy guidance. Asthma has been optimized with prednisone.

redFlags.evidence: Allergy consult 2021 AERD; ED visit 2019; bronchospasm on emergence after ketorolac 2020; ketorolac 30 mg and ibuprofen 600 mg in order set; allergy list says GI upset; bracelet removed.
redFlags.action: Discontinue ketorolac and ibuprofen, update allergy list to respiratory reaction, communicate in time out.

redFlags.evidence: End expiratory wheeze; FeNO 58; FEV1 75%; prednisone bursts.
redFlags.action: Bronchodilator preinduction, deep anesthesia before airway, consider deep extubation or smooth emergence with lidocaine or dexmedetomidine.

redFlags.implication: Hypertension and arrhythmia; beta blockers given for this can precipitate pulmonary edema and bronchospasm.
redFlags.action: Deepen anesthesia or use vasodilator; avoid beta blockers for oxymetazoline hypertension.

redFlags.evidence: MAP 60 to 70 if field bloody; throat pack.
redFlags.action: TIVA with remifentanil, document pack removal.

planItems.item: Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
Acetaminophen and celecoxib; no nonselective NSAIDs

boothComplications.why: Blood in the airway at emergence
